## Design

### 2026-10-06 – ## What I worked on

**3h**

## What I worked on
Designed and finalized the complete hardware schematic for the SmartCurtain controller board, achieving a clean  ERC check and mapping all footprints.

- Integrated ESP32-C3-WROOM-02 with USBC-C input via CH224K sink controller (configured for 12V negotiation) and a Mini360 step-down buck converter to create the 3.3V logic rail
- Added socket headers for the TMC2209 StepStick driver with motor outputs on a 4pin screw terminal, plus dedicated bulk decoupling (100nF)
- Added ambient light and mmWave predisposition
- Added an EC11 rotary encoder for manual input
- Added a PC817 optocoupled output for external triggers and a NPNdriver IR emitter circuit
- Paired every component with his footprints

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WGWQMVpe0ED7g1oQJoTkEXFiLFC2wEVs/fdc42e222085d3e8ee4a4cfbbadc36bfa8f3e41a45e9b59a9e5051e7074f4ac0.png)

## What broke and how I fixed it

- Resolved power net issues where simulation SPICE NPN models caused open emitter /power output ERC errors by swapping to standard KiCad device symbols
- Corrected strapping pin IO9 on the ESP32 (removed floating ground to prevent bootloader lockup)
- Fixed reversed polarity problems on the LED
- Isolated 12v and 3.3V power flags to avoid virtual net shorts

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WGWQMVpe0ED7g1oQJoTkEXFiLFC2wEVs/7a7c5c70dd73296fb40eb62cac5a8b9154685f8485d343b99c7f059f1065a904.png)

### 2026-10-07 – ### What I worked on

**4h**

### What I worked on
Completed the full component placement and traced routing for the SmartCurtain controller board on KiCad, finalizing the PCB ready for fabrication.

### Schematic
- Added M3 Holes for PCB mounting
- Swapped to the full 16 pin dual row footprint for the TMC2209 module to eliminate footprint mismatches

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WGWQMVpe0ED7g1oQJoTkEXFiLFC2wEVs/c1df46bbc1d73668e0479a983dcbad714c1608cf069b86901cec9d6c4309b9fa.png)

### Board Layout
- Positioned the ESP32-C3-WROOM-02 along the board edge, keeping the integrated PCB antenna on the edge
- Aligned all peripheral screw terminals (stepper motor, mmWave radar, light or climate sensor, external triggers...) along the outer perimeter with wire entries facing outwards for clean enclosure passthrough
- Fixed connector clearences in USBC
- Placed the 4x M3 mounting holes away from component housing with the idea to screw them with the stepper motor

### Routing
Initially attempted manual routing, but given the board density and multiple voltage domains, tried running Freerouting as a starting point.
Freerouting handled roughly 20-30% of the initial digital connections, but introduced severe design flaws creating many mistakes (excessive vias, routed high current 12V motor traces with 0.2mm signal widths, and left several uncompleted ratlines).
When reimported into KiCad, the initial DRC flagged over 50 clearence and net violations

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WGWQMVpe0ED7g1oQJoTkEXFiLFC2wEVs/c0b02ece9dde53a3177af529f715b692c70637cf14261432036a69dd6e61a864.png)

### What broke and how I fixed it
- Rerouted 70-80% of the board manually (fixing the errors made by Freerouting(
- Defined custom 0.6mm traces for 12V and 0.4mm for 3.3V
- Resolved `[drill_out_of_range]` errors caused by the default 0.3mm minimum drill with the ESP32 ground path vias by updating board design rules
- Fixed `[copper_edge_clearance]` by tuning Edge.Cuts board outline clearances
- Achived a perfectly clean DRC report with 0 violations, 0 unconnected pads and 0 footprint errors

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WGWQMVpe0ED7g1oQJoTkEXFiLFC2wEVs/5bba32033f435cf9d6af1c5d57a9526186ba90ed0b1fe96b3a7d3dec71b4f30d.png)

### 2026-10-09 – ### What I worked on

**2.5h**

### What I worked on
Conducted electrical trace sizing and thermal validation for the SmartCurtain controller board using KiCad's integrated calculation suite

### Trace Verification
  - Simulated thermal rise under full stepper motor load (1.5A continuous peak current) with standard 1oz (35µm) copper foil thickness.
  - Calculated that an external trace width of 0.525mm results in a conservative temperature rise of only 10°C, a loop resistance of ~0.046Ω, and an insignificant voltage drop of ~0.07V over 50mm.
  - Validated our physical board design: our manual routing of 0.8mm for primary motor supply lines provides a 52% safety margin over IPC-2221 minimums.
- **Electrical Clearance & Creepage:**
  - Evaluated high-voltage insulation tables for USB-C PD 12V-20V potential transients. Verified that our 0.20mm routing clearance comfortably exceeds the required 0.10mm minimum conductor spacing (B2 external conductors).

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WGWQMVpe0ED7g1oQJoTkEXFiLFC2wEVs/4609238272b6816c92c081dc7f02b3723cbf6c78f6e6f913a7e1e085f31074e9.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WGWQMVpe0ED7g1oQJoTkEXFiLFC2wEVs/e9e6d49c2f72fc5c3427bdf4dea48eaddd30e5db28f70c44da4e3466037897e4.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WGWQMVpe0ED7g1oQJoTkEXFiLFC2wEVs/120ecd794d53324f0cae904e673474d0736ff74b2bdd0b80cdd552f8f07d9369.png)

### What broke and how I fixed it
- Discovered an internal-layer routing risk where Freerouting originally attempted to route high-current lines: IPC-2221 calculations revealed that internal traces require 1.367mm width to maintain the same 10°C temperature limit. Ensured all motor coil power traces reside strictly on external copper layers

### Component Placement Data
  - Exported unified centroid coordinate files containing precise footprint center coordinates, package types, and rotation angles.

### 2026-10-10 – ### What I worked on

**2h**

### What I worked on
Solder stencil generation, solder paste aperture optimization, and multi-layer CAM optical inspection.

### Solder Paste Mask Optimization
  - Generated dedicated solder stencil fabrication layers in KiCad Pcbnew.
  - Adjusted global and pad-level paste mask reduction ratios: applied a 10% area reduction (-0.05mm clearance) across the dense 0.5mm-pitch pads of the CH224K SSOP-10 package and USB-C SMD pins. This prevents excessive solder paste deposition, eliminating the risk of accidental solder bridges during hot-plate/reflow soldering.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WGWQMVpe0ED7g1oQJoTkEXFiLFC2wEVs/b022bf9b0c75c95fc095f593a4952eedeab2f470ee601c41af9f178cf61a1ed8.png)

### GerbView
  - Conducted full cross-layer alignment checks in GerbView with differential color overlays.
  - Verified solder mask expansion clearances (set to 0.05mm) against copper pad annular rings, ensuring complete solder dam preservation between closely spaced passive 0805 components.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/WGWQMVpe0ED7g1oQJoTkEXFiLFC2wEVs/14810cd361836766ba086837b6de5bb298557c85568e9d1d698cb9c49ff4fcdb.png)
